Assignments

There are three main assignments in this class: 1) create a dataset, 2) oral exam, and 3) final media analysis project. You must complete all assignments in order to successfully complete this class. There are 160 points available (+3 additional bonus points) across the semester.

AssignmentPointsDue date
Syllabus quiz1 pointSep 11 in class
Reading responses (about one per class, 19 total): for each set of readings, you will have an opportunity to write a ~3-5 sentence response to a given prompt. (This may be during class or at the end of class.)All responses are graded on a ✔️+ (1.5 points), ✔️ (1 pt), ✔️- (0.5 pt) basis = 19 pointsIn class
Attendance and participation: you must speak at least once in class per session in order to receive attendance and participation points (one per class).25 class session = 25 pointsN/A
Assignment 1, Create a dataset (500 words): submit a new dataset, a write-up about the data collection process / what the data shows, and a data visualization of your choice.20 points9 am on Oct 16 (submit to Canvas)
Assignment 2, Midterm oral exam (30 minutes): bring a 1 page handout (guidelines below) and have a conversation about the course material.25 pointsSign up for a 30 minute slot Nov 9–17 (calendar link TBD). One-page handout is due online 24 hours before your slot; submit PDF to Canvas, bring hard copy to exam.
Assignment 3, Media analysis project: choose a media phenomenon, topic, controversy, etc. and systematically gather data about, code/categorize the data in some way, visualize the data, and analyze your findings.  
(3.1) Project brainstorm (1 slide): add no more than 3 ideas to shared deck. Be prepared to speak for ~3 min.3 pointsOct 7 or 9 (date assigned in advance, slide deck link TBD)
(3.2) Project proposal and annotated bibliography (1000 words): submit a 600 word proposal about what you will study and how you propose to do so. Attach a 400 word annotated bibliography with at least 7 sources.10 points9 am on Oct 23; submit on Canvas
(3.3) Research progress meeting (30 min): discuss your project proposal, bibliography, and how the themes in class relate to your project. Booking link TBD.5 pointsSign up for a 30-minute slot Oct 28–Nov 6
(3.4) First draft (at least 2000 words): submit the written first draft of your final project.10 points9 am on Nov 13
(3.5) Peer review of first draft (oral): present draft of the video/demo portions of the assignment. Critique 2 of your colleagues’ work.5 pointsIn class on Nov 13 or 18 (assigned in advance)
(3.6) Two peer review memos (written, 350 words each): after reading all of the materials, write a review memo for each person about the project’s strengths and points of improvement.5 points9 am, Nov 25 (submit on Canvas)
(3.7) Personal review (at least 350 words): read the peer reviews (and AI reviews, if applicable) and write a response. What will you change (or not change) based on the comments?2 points9 am, Dec 4 (submit on Canvas)
(3.8) Written final draft (at least 2500 words)15 points9 am, Dec 4 (submit on Canvas)
(3.9) Oral presentation (5-minute video or PechaKucha)15 pointsIn class on Dec 4 or 9 (date assigned in advance)
Bonus assignments: make an appointment at the writing center or during my office hours. Submit screenshots of the confirmation emails to this Google Form.1 point each (3 point cap)9 am, Dec 4
TOTAL AVAILABLE POINTS160 points (+3 bonus) = 163 

Grading schema: A ≥ 140 · B ≥ 124 · C ≥ 108 · D ≥ 92 · F < 92 (out of 160)
